chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ asked him about the case of a man who forgot to give the adhān and iqāmah until he pronounced the takbīr and entered into the salat (prayer). He said: If he had entered the mosque with the intention that he would give the adhān and the iqāmah, then he should continue in his salat (prayer) and not turn away.

key_terms.يَنْصَرِفْ: he should not turn away or leave
key_terms.يُؤَذِّنَ: to recite the adhān, the call to prayer
key_terms.يُقِيمَ: to recite the iqāmah, the commencement call before prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets the adhān and iqāmah until after starting salat (prayer), should he continue or stop?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgot the adhān and iqāmah until after beginning the salat (prayer). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if he had entered the mosque already intending to perform them, then he should continue the prayer and not break it. The narration is significant in prayer rulings concerning forgetfulness and the effect of prior niyyah (intention).
